transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I... well, I hope I'm not taking up time someone else might need more, but my family thought it would be best if I spoke to someone. 

What brings me in is just... well, since my friend was killed, I've been having a bit of a hard time. I really have been trying to move on and be strong, I promise. But I've just been living with this constant mix of... well, fear, mostly. And, um... I feel terrible even admitting this, but also a lot of guilt and anger. I know I shouldn't be so angry, and I try very hard not to be, but it's just always there. 

It just hasn't eased up the way everyone seemed to think it would by now. I've really been trying to handle it well on my own, but I just can't seem to shake it. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining things properly.
Since your friend’s death, have you found yourself feeling constantly on edge, easily startled, or overly watchful of your surroundings?

Well, um... I suppose I have been a little bit more watchful than I used to be. I don't want to sound paranoid or anything, I really don't. It's just... whenever I'm near traffic now, I find myself watching everything so closely. 

I watch every truck, every curb, every pedestrian... it almost feels like it's my responsibility to catch the danger before it happens again. I know that probably sounds silly, and I try not to let it show, but I just can't seem to turn it off. Is it normal to feel that way? I hope I'm not overreacting to things.
Have you noticed yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities that remind you of your friend’s death?

Well, um... I do try to be flexible and not let things get in the way of my normal routine, I really do. But... I suppose I have been making a few changes. 

I feel a bit foolish admitting this, because I know it's probably silly, but I actually go out of my way now to avoid that specific intersection. It adds time to my drive, and I know I should just push through it, but I just... I can't quite bring myself to go through there right now. 

And, oh, I feel terrible about this because I used to be so involved, but I've also stopped signing up for most of the group tours and the community safety meetings. I just... I cannot bear it when the conversations inevitably circle back to what happened there. I don't want to make a scene or make anyone else uncomfortable if I get upset, so it just seems better for everyone if I stay home. 

I hope it's okay that I'm just stepping back from those things for a little while. Is that a normal way to handle it, or am I just running away from my problems?
Since your friend’s death, have you found yourself feeling guilty or angry most days, even when you try not to?

Well, um... I really do try my best to stay positive, I promise I do. I know it doesn't do anyone any good to dwell on things. But... yes, I suppose I do feel a bit of both, more often than I'd like. 

I feel so awful even saying it, because I know it was an accident, but I just get so angry sometimes. Not at anyone in particular, just... angry that it happened. And the guilt... oh, I try to tell myself there was nothing I could have done, but it just sits there in the back of my mind. I really am working on letting it go, though. I don't want to be a bitter person. Is it terrible that I haven't been able to just move past it yet? I hope you don't think poorly of me for feeling this way.
How long have you been feeling this way — the fear, guilt, and anger — since your friend’s death? Has it been more than a month?

Well, um... yes, it has been more than a month. I hope I'm not taking too long to get over it, I really don't want to be a burden on anyone. But... it's actually been going on ever since it happened. 

My friend was killed on that walking tour about two years and three months ago. I know that sounds like a terribly long time to still be struggling with all of this, and I feel a bit embarrassed admitting it's been that long. I really have been trying my hardest to move on and be strong, I promise I have. Is it... is it very unusual to still be feeling this way after two years? I just want to make sure I'm not doing something wrong in how I'm handling it.
Do you find yourself having strong emotional reactions, like sudden sadness or anger, when you think about what happened to your friend or when something reminds you of it?

Well, um... I really try to keep a level head, I do. I know it's not helpful to get all worked up, especially when there are people around. I try very hard to just... keep things pleasant. 

But, I suppose... well, I haven't really noticed any big outbursts or anything like that. I mean, I might get a little quiet sometimes if a memory pops up, but I certainly try not to let myself get suddenly angry or overwhelmed. I wouldn't want to make anyone else uncomfortable or draw attention to myself. 

I just try to take a deep breath and push through it, you know? I hope that's the right way to handle it. I really am trying to be sensible about the whole thing. Does that sound okay to you?

The duration of symptoms exceeding two years supports chronicity, but no clear evidence of delayed onset or other specifiers was identified to narrow the diagnosis further.
